title: [ORION-QG QG-19] Universal trade/test-set calculus for compiler regime geometry
body:
Parent programme: #740
Frontier basis: QG-7/QG-7b/QG-7c trade ladder, QG-8/QG-16 objective cones, QG-9 V6 whole-system relocation, QG-13 theorem mining.

## Status

**WAVE-3 STRUCTURAL FRONTIER — determine whether a fixed compiler family admits an objective-independent finite set of primitive semantics-preserving moves that certifies global optimality across all linear resource objectives.**

ORION-QG currently discovers elementary trades empirically/theorem-by-theorem: split, borrow, phantom borrow, split+borrow hybrid, local deletions, combined deletions, and whole-system Tag relocation. QG-8/QG-16 then derive objective cones in which selected moves are non-increasing. What is still missing is the converse structural object:

> Is there a finite, objective-independent **compiler test set** T such that for every feasible but non-optimal compilation x and every admitted linear objective theta, at least one feasible move t in T strictly improves theta·r(x)?

If such a T exists and stabilizes with system size, the regime geometry is no longer merely a discovered list of trade families: it has a universal primitive move basis. If it does not exist, the failure mode identifies exactly why context-dependent/global compiler moves are irreducible.

## Strong donor subtraction

This lane gives zero novelty credit to the underlying mathematics.

- Graver (1975) and subsequent integer-programming theory establish universal test sets/Graver bases for integer programs.
- Circuit directions are universal test directions for linear programming; Graver elements play the integer analogue.
- Discrete convex analysis/M-convexity gives exchange axioms and local-to-global optimality criteria for special discrete feasible sets.
- Gröbner/Markov/Graver bases, Hilbert bases, augmentation algorithms, and normal-fan geometry are donor mathematics.

Relevant modern pointers include Onn's 2024 work on circuit/Graver walks and current 2026 work on practical Graver-basis extraction; these do not by themselves establish that ORION-QG compiler fibers admit a fixed lifted integer representation or a stabilizing compiler test set.

Candidate contribution is restricted to a **compiler-specific proof-carrying test-set representation**, or a first-class refutation showing that the frozen quantum compilation semantics require context-dependent/non-stabilizing moves.

## Q1 — lifted semantic fiber

For one frozen ORION-QG family, construct an exact integer/lattice encoding of feasible compilations:

`F(b) = { x in Z^m : A x = b, l <= x <= u, x satisfies declared lifted integrality constraints }`

with a linear resource map `r(x)=R x + r0` whenever possible.

The encoding must preserve, without relaxation:
- Pauli/symplectic acceptance;
- shared Tag labels/syndromes;
- dependent-frame recomputation;
- central-branch choice;
- Restore/F3 accounting;
- block permutations and any declared discrete branch selectors.

XOR/parity conditions may be lifted with integer carry variables. A nonlinear semantic coupling that cannot be represented without instance-dependent structure is itself a result.

Start with **R6I** because its production DP is additive/min-plus and the V6 theorem exposes a global relocation move; use **R6M TARE** second because F3/shared-Tag coupling is the harder stress case.

## Q2 — primitive kernel move extraction

For bounded n=2..4 exact domains:
1. enumerate feasible-state differences `g = y-x` with `A g = 0`;
2. quotient exact symmetries;
3. extract conformally/minimally indecomposable moves under the frozen lifted representation;
4. compare the resulting primitive classes against known ORION-QG moves:
   - R6S deletion/exchange;
   - QG-7 split/borrow/phantom/hybrid trades;
   - QG-13 E2/E3 combined deletions;
   - QG-9 V6 whole-system Tag relocation.

Do **not** assume the known QG trade list is complete. Missing primitive classes are new candidate compiler moves; known trades absent from the kernel representation falsify the representation or reveal context dependence.

## Q3 — objective-independent optimality test

For each bounded exact instance/objective family, freeze T before scoring and test:

> `x` is globally optimal iff no feasible augmentation `x + lambda g` with `g in T`, `lambda>0`, strictly reduces the exact objective.

Use exact unrestricted DP/enumeration only as hidden referee after the no-improving-move prediction is sealed.

Required controls:
- all known positive QG trade witnesses must expose at least one improving primitive move;
- exact optima must expose none;
- random objective coefficients plus QG-8/QG-16 boundary/equality points;
- deliberately outside-cone objectives from QG-2/QG-17.

## Q4 — stabilization with n

A bounded test set is not an all-n result. Ask whether primitive move **types modulo qubit permutation/local Pauli relabeling** stabilize:

`T_2 subseteq T_3 subseteq ... -> finite orbit basis T_*`

Strong positive target:

> beyond a proved support/locality radius k, every primitive improving move embeds an orbit representative from T_*.

Possible proof routes are donor-owned: n-fold/block-structured IP stabilization, finite-support normal forms, Steinitz/Davenport arguments, or compiler-specific locality/exchange lemmas.

A growth witness is equally important: if new primitive move orbit types appear unboundedly with n, serialize the minimal growth mechanism.

## Q5 — relation to objective phase geometry

For every primitive resource delta `Delta r(g)`, the sign change occurs on

`theta · Delta r(g) = 0`.

Compare the arrangement generated by the test-set deltas against:
- QG-8 support-two cone facets;
- QG-16 support-one cone facets;
- QG-17 finite sharpness hyperplanes;
- known TARE trade-regime boundaries.

If all true objective phase changes are generated by primitive test-set deltas, ORION-QG obtains an exact route from **move basis -> hyperplane arrangement -> regime cells**. If not, preserve the counterexample and identify the missing composite/context-dependent mechanism.

## Q6 — M-convex/exchange diagnostic

Test whether any exact compiler resource/feasible-set projection satisfies a recognized discrete-convex exchange axiom. This is a donor classification exercise, not a novelty claim.

- Positive: local exchange optimality can replace some global referees and sharply explain finite trade bases.
- Negative: serialize the smallest exchange-axiom counterexample; the obstruction may explain why global relocation/coupling moves are required.

## Independent verification

Generic ORION:
- rebuild the lifted semantic encoding from primitive Pauli/compiler rules;
- independently enumerate primitive bounded moves;
- verify every claimed augmentation and resource delta;
- compare no-improving-move certificates against hidden exact referees only after sealing.

Native ORION-Q:
- keep `BOUNDED_TEST_SET`, `ALL_N_STABILIZATION`, `OBJECTIVE_PHASE_GENERATION`, and `REPRESENTATION_FAILURE` as separate authority coordinates;
- never infer all-n completeness from finite n saturation;
- never infer novelty from correspondence with Graver/circuit theory.

## Strong terminals

- `QG19_COMPILER_UNIVERSAL_TEST_SET_SUPPORTED_ON_FROZEN_FAMILY`
- `QG19_PRIMITIVE_MOVE_ORBITS_STABILIZE_ALL_N_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG19_OBJECTIVE_PHASE_BOUNDARIES_GENERATED_BY_TEST_SET_DELTAS`
- `QG19_NEW_PRIMITIVE_COMPILER_MOVE_CLASS_FOUND`

Honest alternatives:
- `QG19_FIXED_KERNEL_REPRESENTATION_REFUTED__CONTEXT_DEPENDENT_MOVE_REQUIRED`
- `QG19_PRIMITIVE_MOVE_TYPES_GROW_WITH_N`
- `QG19_DISCRETE_CONVEX_EXCHANGE_REFUTED`
- `QG19_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Literature anchors / donor boundary

- J. E. Graver, *On the foundations of linear and linear integer programming I*, Mathematical Programming 9 (1975).
- S. Onn, *Nonlinear Discrete Optimization* (2010/2011); Graver bases as fundamental augmenting/test directions.
- S. Onn, *Circuit and Graver Walks and Linear and Integer Programming*, arXiv:2410.00656 (2024).
- K. Murota, *Discrete Convex Analysis*; M-convex exchange and local-to-global criteria.
- Recent Graver extraction work (2026) is methodology prior art only.

No physical quantum-advantage claim follows. The protected stretched-N2 subject remains sealed. Existing frozen QG protocols/results are read-only parents; this issue authorizes only a fresh prospective protocol.
